exposure: combined spinal-epidural anesthesia and epidural analgesia
cohort: The study included 137 preeclamptic women who underwent painless delivery at The Second People's Hospital of Linhai City between July 2022 and July 2024.
finding: Combined spinal-epidural anesthesia and epidural analgesia significantly accelerated labor, relieved pain, lowered blood pressure, improved serum indicators, and decreased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to Doula delivery analgesia in preeclamptic women.
mod_finding: The group receiving combined spinal-epidural anesthesia and epidural analgesia had a lower rate of cesarean section compared to the Doula delivery analgesia group.
